description: This part of Non-Verbal Logical Reasoning involves finding similarities between figures and identifying the odd one out. It tests a candidate's visual perception and pattern recognition skills.

sections.title: Figure Analogy
sections.description: In this, a specific relationship is established between a pair of figures, and the unknown figure must be found by applying the exact same relationship to the second pair.

key_concepts.explanation: Just as figure A is related to figure B, logically figure C must be related to figure D in exactly the same way.
The shifting of internal symbols or lines in a specific, predictable sequence while transitioning from one figure to another.

sections.title: Figure Classification
sections.description: Also known as 'Odd One Out'. Several figures are provided, out of which all except one share a common underlying similarity.

key_concepts.explanation: Forming a group of figures that follow a common rule, such as having the same number of sides or identical shading patterns.
The single figure among the given multiple-choice options that breaks or fails to follow the established rule of the group.

sections.title: Common Rules of Transformation
sections.description: The primary logical rules used to understand changes and patterns in figures, highly useful in both analogy and classification questions.

results: Rotating figures in a clockwise direction (e.g., 45°, 90°, 180°).
Rotating figures in an anti-clockwise direction by a specific, constant angle.
A sequential increase in the number of lines, dots, or sides of the main figures.
A systematic decrease or deletion of outer or inner elements.
Forming a mirror image of the figure (laterally inverted left to right).
Forming a water image of the figure (vertically inverted top to bottom).

sections.title: Steps to Solve Questions
sections.description: A systematic process to solve figure-based Analogy and Classification questions accurately and quickly.

steps.title: Observe the Figures Carefully
steps.detail: Analyze the main body of the figure and the smaller elements (like dots, arrows, pins) located inside or outside it separately.

steps.title: Identify the Pattern of Change
steps.detail: Discover the specific mathematical or spatial rule governing the change in size, direction, position, or number of elements.

steps.title: Eliminate from Options
steps.detail: Immediately eliminate the answer choices that clearly do not follow the identified rule to easily narrow down to the correct answer.
